questions.stem: At terminal velocity, what is true about the forces on a falling object?

options.text: The driving force is greater than drag
Weight equals drag (air resistance), so resultant force is zero

questions.explanation: At terminal velocity, the drag force has increased to exactly match the weight. The resultant force is zero, so there is no acceleration and the object falls at constant velocity.

questions.stem: Which of the following would NOT reduce the drag force on a car?

options.text: Increasing the mass of the car

questions.explanation: Drag depends on speed, shape, surface area, and the fluid's density -- not on the mass of the object. Increasing the car's mass has no direct effect on drag force (though it would affect the car's acceleration).
